# Multikey index coverage and multiKeyPaths
Source: https://llms-explorer.com/tree/multikey-index-coverage-and-multikeypaths/

# Multikey index coverage and multiKeyPaths — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Multikey index coverage and multiKeyPaths. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-24 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] For an index {genres:1,title:1} where genres is an array and title is scalar, find({genres:"Drama"},{_id:0,title:1}) is a covered-query pattern; including genres in the returned projection prevents coverage. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md · keywords: Multikey index coverage and multiKeyPaths · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md

## Structure and components

- [statement] A compound multikey index can cover a query that filters an array and returns indexed non-array fields, provided the array is excluded from the result, the query contains no $elemMatch, and the other covered-query requirements hold. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md · keywords: Multikey index coverage and multiKeyPaths · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md
- [statement] multiKeyPaths identifies array-bearing components separately for each indexed field. For example, {field1:[],field2:["field2"]} marks only field2 as multikey even though isMultiKey is true for the compound index. This makes field-level inspection more informative than the index-wide flag alone. (medium confidence) — https://dev.to/franckpachot/mongodb-multikey-indexes-and-index-bound-optimization-ol9 · keywords: Multikey index coverage and multiKeyPaths · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md
- [statement] An indexed dotted field can have multikey ancestry even if its terminal value is scalar. The worked example records obj.sub2:['obj'] when obj becomes an array, while obj.sub1 records both obj and obj.sub1 when both levels contain arrays. (low confidence) — https://dev.to/franckpachot/mongodb-multikey-indexes-and-index-bound-optimization-ol9
- [statement] A multikey index stores separate entries for distinct array values, with multiple entries potentially pointing to one document; MongoDB automatically makes an index multikey when indexed data contains arrays. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md · keywords: Multikey index coverage and multiKeyPaths · also: https://www.percona.com/sites/default/files/presentations/Indexes-MongoDB.pdf

## How it works

- [statement] An array ancestor can make a dotted indexed field multikey even when its leaf values are scalar. In Pachot's worked example, an array at obj produces multiKeyPaths["obj.sub2"]=["obj"]. Inspect ancestors as well as the projected leaf. (low confidence) — https://dev.to/franckpachot/mongodb-multikey-indexes-and-index-bound-optimization-ol9
- [statement] Coverage requires all predicate and returned fields to be available from the same index; exclude _id explicitly when it is not indexed. Satisfying these field requirements alone does not remove the additional multikey restrictions. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md · keywords: Multikey index coverage and multiKeyPaths · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] To verify coverage in a classic explain plan, check for an index projection without FETCH and totalDocsExamined:0. An IXSCAN alone proves index access, not index-only execution; the worked coverage tutorial shows both IXSCAN-plus-FETCH and PROJECTION_COVERED plans. (low confidence) — https://dev.to/mongodb/index-only-scan-on-json-documents-with-covering-and-multi-key-indexes-in-mongodb-53h4
- [statement] Use explain("executionStats") to verify document avoidance. For the documented IXSCAN/FETCH plan representation, a covered scan has no FETCH ancestor of IXSCAN and examines zero collection documents. Check the plan as well as totalDocsExamined, especially for empty results. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md · keywords: Multikey index coverage and multiKeyPaths · also: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48351679/mongodb-covered-query-is-not-able-to-satisfy-query-from-index

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] SERVER-130777 reports a resumable-build failure in which an array-producing side write arrives after the collection scan, a clean restart loses its in-memory multikey state, and the committed index is incorrectly flagged non-multikey. The report describes missed results and covered projections returning an array element. Treat this as a reported failure mode, not a verified claim that every deployment of the listed versions is affected. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-12) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-130777

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] One engineering tutorial's text says that projecting phoneNumber from a scalar document remains covered after another document makes phoneNumber multikey, but its own printed explain output shows PROJECTION_SIMPLE, FETCH and totalDocsExamined:1. That example supports checking the plan rather than trusting its heading. (low confidence) — https://dev.to/mongodb/index-only-scan-on-json-documents-with-covering-and-multi-key-indexes-in-mongodb-53h4
- [statement] The historical MongoDB 3.6.0 reproduction reports isMultiKey:false and multiKeyPaths containing an empty array for address.zipcode. Its hinted plan uses IXSCAN and reports totalDocsExamined:0. This illustrates plan selection versus coverage capability, rather than a multikey coverage failure. (low confidence) — https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48351679/mongodb-covered-query-is-not-able-to-satisfy-query-from-index

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The multikey manual excludes queries containing $elemMatch from coverage. A historical Stack Overflow answer explains that index keys alone may not distinguish an array of subdocuments from a scalar embedded document with the same indexed values; the question prints a FETCH stage for its $elemMatch reproduction. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md · keywords: Multikey index coverage and multiKeyPaths · also: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/47473283/when-using-elemmatch-why-is-mongodb-performing-a-fetch-stage-if-index-is-cover
- [statement] Multikey indexing can create multiple index entries per document. Percona's original experiment used a 100-element indexed array and described 100 index operations per insertion; this illustrates fan-out, not a transferable performance ratio for current MongoDB. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md · keywords: Multikey index coverage and multiKeyPaths · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/532x-multikey-index-insertion-performance-increase-for-mongodb-with-fractal-tree-indexes/
- [statement] For exact equality to an entire array, a multikey index can narrow candidates using the first query-array element, but MongoDB must fetch candidates to verify the complete array; indexing all named fields does not make this predicate covered. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md
- [statement] Index coverage does not independently guarantee an index-provided array sort. The manual requires full [MinKey,MaxKey] bounds for all sort fields and no multikey-bound path prefix shared with the sort pattern to avoid an in-memory sort. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md
- [statement] The validate method documents inconsistencies where an index has multikeyPaths for non-multikey fields, lacks paths for multikey documents in an older index, or is marked multikey without multikey fields. Metadata consistency is therefore a distinct diagnostic concern. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.validate.md
- [statement] Multikey does not categorically prohibit coverage. A compound multikey index can cover eligible queries that return indexed non-array fields, provided path-level multikey information is available and the other covered-query requirements hold. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md · keywords: Multikey index coverage and multiKeyPaths · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md
- [statement] The documented multikey coverage conditions exclude queries containing $elemMatch. Adding $elemMatch to improve array-element matching does not establish index-only execution. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md
